page: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.8xlarge instance is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processors running at a base clock frequency of 2.5 GHz on x86_64 architecture. Managed via a KVM hypervisor, this instance features 16 physical CPU cores configured with hyper-threading to provide 32 vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU core. The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, BMI2, and FMA, backed by a 35 MB L3 cache alongside 1.0 MB L2 cache per core. The server operates with a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no local NVMe SSD storage, and includes no attached GPUs.

Performance benchmarks position the instance primarily in the middle 50% tier across multi-core and memory workloads, while single-core processing demonstrates lower relative throughput. The stress-ng multi-core CPU score reaches 28006.29 alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 10179.0. Conversely, single-core benchmarks evaluate in the bottom 25%, with stress-ng single-core achieving 1311.98 and single-threaded gzip compression registering 22.62 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth testing records 108.04 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 47.67 GB/sec for uncached writes. The lack of integrated local storage necessitates reliance on cloud network-attached block storage for persistent data requirements.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM allocation provides a balanced resource profile for multi-threaded enterprise services that do not demand dedicated local storage or GPU acceleration. The aggregate multi-core throughput and memory capacity make this instance suitable for general-purpose application servers, container orchestration nodes, Redis caching layers (benchmarked at 26.79 million SET operations/sec), web serving (achieving 20.21 GB/sec static throughput), and intermediate database workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz under the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs with hyper-threading, paired with 128.0 GB of system memory to maintain a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Hardware instruction support includes AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, and FMA. Benchmark results place multi-core CPU and memory performance in the middle 50% tier, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 10179.0 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 130.22 GB/sec. Single-core performance falls in the bottom 25% percentile. The instance provides 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, lacks integrated local storage, and contains no GPUs. This hardware balance suits general application workloads, microservice hosting, Redis caching, static web serving, and database operations relying on attached network storage.
